title: Generative Latent Diffusion for Efficient Spatiotemporal Data Reduction
problem: Generative models offer compression but lack controllability and reconstruction accuracy for practical data compression; existing compressors (SZ3) have limited compression ratios
motivation: Scientific simulations produce massive spatiotemporal datasets; improving compression ratios while maintaining reconstruction accuracy enables better data management
method: This method combines two neural network techniques: a VAE (which compresses data into a compact 'latent space' representation) and a conditional diffusion model (which reconstructs images by gradually reducing noise, guided by specific conditions). Instead of compressing every frame of video, it stores only keyframes—the key visual moments—in their compressed latent form. The diffusion model then fills in all the frames between keyframes by learning to predict what they should look like based on those stored keyframes. By storing only compressed keyframes rather than compressing every single frame, this achieves much higher compression ratios.
key_novelty: Combining VAE and diffusion models to store only compressed keyframes and reconstruct the rest, achieving better compression than generative methods that compress every frame separately.
contributions: VAE+conditional diffusion architecture for spatiotemporal compression
Keyframe-based latent storage reducing storage overhead
10x compression ratio vs SZ3 across datasets
63% better performance vs learning-based methods at same error
limitations: Model training cost not quantified; keyframe selection strategy not detailed; evaluation datasets not fully specified; inference latency not discussed
